title: Operator ordering as an emergent gauge field in twisted bilayer graphene: singular spectral signatures at the magic angle
abstract: Scanning-tunnelling spectroscopy at the AB and BA stacking points of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene should reveal two asymmetric Van~Hove peaks separated by $Δ_{\mathrm{split}}\approx 171$~meV -- a splitting absent from the standard Bistritzer--MacDonald spectrum. We show this signature arises naturally from the Hermitian ordering correction of the Dirac Hamiltonian with spatially varying mass, which generates an emergent Aharonov--Bohm flux of $h/(2e)$ at each zero of the effective mass $m_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{r})=w|f(\mathbf{r})|$. In the chiral limit, the interlayer coupling is locally diagonalised by a spatially dependent unitary transformation; the ordering term $H_{\mathrm{ord}}=-\tfrac{i}{2}\boldsymbolσ\cdot \nabla\ln m_{\mathrm{eff}}$ then develops a $1/r$ singularity at the AB/BA stacking points, where $m_{\mathrm{eff}}$ vanishes. The splitting scales as $\sqrtθ$ -- distinguishing it from correlation-driven gaps ($\proptoθ$ or $\propto 1/θ$) -- is gate-voltage independent, and is spatially localised within $r_c\approx 2.1$~nm of each AB/BA point. Within the local asymptotic theory near the zeros of $\mathrm{eff}$, the ordering-corrected zero mode acquires parabolic-cylinder character $D_{-1/2}$. The spatially resolved AB/BA spectrum reported in recent STM studies of magic-angle TBG has not been analysed for two-peak structure and constitutes an immediate experimental test; the predicted cell-averaged broadening of $\approx 14$~meV is consistent with the $16$~meV discrepancy between existing STM data and the BM tight-binding prediction.
summary: This theoretical work predicts that the spectral features of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene are governed by an operator ordering correction term. This correction acts like an emergent Aharonov–Bohm flux at stacking boundaries, lifting degeneracy and causing a measurable splitting ($\approx 171$ meV) in the electronic density of states. The finding provides a unique, geometrically derived signature for experimental verification using STM spectroscopy.
main_problem: To determine the spectral signatures at the AB/BA stacking points of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) that are absent from standard continuum models.
main_result: The required Hermitian ordering correction to the Dirac Hamiltonian generates an emergent Aharonov–Bohm flux, splitting the zero-energy degeneracy into two asymmetric Van Hove peaks separated by $\Delta_{	ext{split}} \approx 171$ meV.
method: The analysis involves deriving the necessary self-adjoint extension of the continuum Dirac operator and solving the resulting radial equations near mass zeros using adiabatic interpolation techniques.
model_or_system: The system is magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) modeled by a continuum Dirac Hamiltonian. The key theoretical development is incorporating an ordering term, $H_{	ext{ord}}$, which restores functional-analytic Hermiticity due to spatially varying mass profiles.
key_observables: Two asymmetric Van Hove peaks separated by $\Delta_{	ext{split}} \approx 171$ meV; the scaling of this splitting as $\sqrt{	heta}$.
important_parameters: Magic angle ($	heta$), effective mass $m_{	ext{eff}}(\mathbf{r})$, and the emergent flux quantum $h/(2e)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that spectral structure is governed by the self-adjoint extension of the Dirac operator, requiring adherence to current conservation and square-integrability of zero modes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate adiabatic evolution showing gap splitting; LDOS maps show two distinct peaks at AB/BA points; and a plot confirms $\Delta_{	ext{split}}$ scales with $\sqrt{	heta}$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the failure of naive Hamiltonians to conserve current, deriving the necessary ordering correction ($H_{	ext{ord}}$), mathematically proving its physical necessity via self-adjoint extensions, and finally predicting measurable spectral signatures ($\Delta_{	ext{split}}$) at specific stacking points.
why_interesting: The mechanism relies on subtle mathematical requirements (self-adjointness, current conservation) applied to a condensed matter system, linking geometric topology (emergent flux) directly to observable electronic structure in strongly correlated materials.
